Benefits: Base salary, Bonus, Social insurance and housing funds, Medical check-up, EAP Program.

Responsible For: Providing field service for UPS power systems: installing, configuring and commissioning them, and completing field service assignments and bench repair jobs end to end. Required Skills and Experience Hands-on experience with UPS power systems from 1 kVA to and above 500 kVA, including large, tower, modular and edge UPS installations. Clear understanding of single-phase and three-phase electrical systems, three-phase power distribution, and grounding systems. Data center site survey and load calculation skills. Ability to provide SLA support with customer satisfaction. Good communication skills and the confidence to deal with customers directly. Preferred OEM Certifications and Training Completions: Level 1 Field Support certifications on the UPS power systems product line of one or more of the OEMs mentioned below: Vertiv (formerly Emerson) and Liebert – e.g. Field Engineer Level 1 Schneider (formerly APC) – e.g. EcoXpert Foundation, Field Service 1, etc. Eaton e.g. Eaton Foundation, Field Engineer 1, etc. Huawei (Digital Power) - Power Foundation, Commissioning 1, HCSA-Field-Data Center Facility (H20-913), etc. Expected Knowledge: The engineer works within the critical power infrastructure around the UPS. Core means hands-on ownership; Working means able to work with and troubleshoot at the interface to the UPS. LV Switchgear - ACB, MCCB, MCB, busbar systems Energy Storage - VRLA, lithium-ion, Ni-Cd, flywheel, battery monitoring Power Distribution - MDB, SMDB, DB, busway / busduct, PDU, RPP, rack PDU Critical Power Architecture - Single feed, dual feed, A/B power, N, N+1, 2N, 2N+1 Power Monitoring - UPS and PDU monitoring, branch circuit monitoring, smart meters UPS - Online double conversion, modular, centralized, static and rotary UPS; N / N+1, 2N, 2N+1 Protection and Safety - Earthing, grounding, SPD, overcurrent and short circuit protection, arc flash Power Quality - Harmonics, power factor, voltage regulation, surge protection, transients, power conditioning Commissioning and Testing - FAT, SAT, load bank testing, UPS and protection testing, integrated systems testing Tasks and Responsibilities Technical Service and Installation Provide field service for UPS power systems. Install, configure and commission UPS power systems, including large UPS installations and edge UPS. Install power equipment and carry out the related electrical services. Provide technical service and DC power services. Carry out data center site surveys and load calculations. Troubleshoot to component level using sound troubleshooting protocols and frameworks. Provide SLA support. Field Service Attend customer calls promptly and professionally. Before leaving for the client site, make sure the problem is fully understood, and carry the required tools and spare parts. Remain polite, helpful and courteous with the customer, and confirm the customer is satisfied before leaving the site. Check the electrical and environmental condition at the client site (power, earthing, cooling) and inform the office if it is found unsuitable. Inform the FDO of the billing amount and all details required to raise an invoice, wherever applicable. Inform the FDO of any commitment made to a customer during a call so that follow-up action can be taken. Such commitments must be clearly highlighted in the FSR. If a customer asks for work outside the company’s service obligations, obtain approval from the office before carrying it out. On return to the office, hand over the office copy of the FSR to the FDO for data entry and dispatch to Head Office for record keeping. Workshop / Bench Repair Receive repair jobs from the front desk along with a properly filled job card. Verify that the parts requested are genuinely required and, in the quantity, requested. Prepare estimates for customer jobs and send them to the customer for approval; start a repair only after the approved estimate is received. Ensure every job is completed in all respects and tested before handover. Prevent repeat complaints caused by negligence, inefficiency or poor workmanship. Administration and Conduct Maintain a professional attitude toward work, colleagues and clients. Be self-motivated in promoting the company’s business and services. Observe punctuality and discipline. Follow company rules, regulations and policies in letter and spirit. Interaction Coordinate with Head Office for report submission and company data as and when required.
